clue.text: Visitor to theatre put oomph into actor

parts.note: an actor is a player on the stage
oomph or energy is go, as in full of go

explanation.surface: A director urges more energy from a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who attends plays at a theatre is a regular theatre audience member.

clue.text: Rubbish heap has leaves in it

indicators.note: has leaves in it means the leaves word sits inside the heap word

parts.note: a heap is a pile
FF is the abbreviation for folios, the leaves of a book

explanation.surface: A pile of garden waste full of fallen leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like foliage but is pages: ff. stands for folios.
explanation.definitionFit: Piffle is nonsense, talk that is rubbish.

clue.text: Poorly containing BSE is one way of reaching rock bottom

definitions.text: one way of reaching rock bottom

indicators.note: containing means the poorly word holds the letters BSE inside

parts.note: someone poorly is ailing

explanation.surface: A sick cow with mad cow disease sinks to its lowest point.
explanation.walkthrough: BSE is bovine spongiform encephalopathy, mad cow disease; 'rock bottom' is the foot of a cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: Abseiling is descending a rock face on a rope.

clue.text: Greek in Sweden smiles

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: A Greek visitor to Sweden is beaming.
explanation.definitionFit: Grins are broad smiles.

clue.text: The Spanish people topless? It's high spirits

parts.note: a people is a nation

explanation.surface: Spaniards sunbathing topless are in great spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is joyful exhilaration, a feeling of being on top of the world.

clue.text: Man is one and no man is one (Donne)

definitions.meaning: the Isle of Man is a piece of land in the sea
John Donne wrote that no man is an ..., entire of itself

explanation.surface: A philosophical musing quoting the poet John Donne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland; Donne's famous line then supplies the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is surrounded by sea, and Donne's meditation says no person is isolated in that way.

clue.text: Soft drink and Adam's ale sometimes put in whisky

parts.note: soda is a fizzy soft drink
Adam's ale is a jocular name for plain water

explanation.surface: Mixers to add to a glass of Scotch.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky and soda is a classic mix of the spirit with fizzy carbonated liquid.

clue.text: Last five spoilt the celebration

explanation.definitionFit: A festival is a period of public celebration and feasting.

clue.text: Clever commercial tosh takes one in

one as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A clever advertisement that is still nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and quick-witted, so clever in a deft way.

parts.note: up to this point means so far
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in Rex or Regina

explanation.surface: So far the monarch has had no throne.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa is an upholstered seat for several people.

clue.text: Cuts taken from buffalo in season

indicators.note: taken from says the letters are lifted out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Meat taken from buffalo hunted in season.
explanation.definitionFit: Loins are cuts of meat from an animal's lower back, such as pork loin.

clue.text: Press operates effectively where metal is smelted

parts.note: to press clothes is to iron them
something that operates effectively works

explanation.surface: A machine press runs smoothly in a foundry.
explanation.definitionFit: An ironworks is a factory where iron is smelted and wrought.

clue.text: Draw off drink in small amounts, getting hot working

parts.note: to sip is to drink in small amounts
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Sipping a drink slowly while getting heated at work.
explanation.definitionFit: To siphon a liquid is to draw it off through a tube.

clue.text: Tricks gangster with eye signals

parts.note: a hood is a gangster, short for hoodlum
winks are signals made by closing one eye

explanation.surface: A mobster deceives using knowing glances.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoodwink is to deceive or trick.

clue.text: Unusually quaint English relic

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of quaint are arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An odd, charming old English artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: An antique is an old object surviving from the past, a relic of earlier times.

clue.text: Small musical group after two pints gets boundlessly better

indicators.note: after places the trimmed word following the quart

parts.note: a quart is two pints

indicators.note: boundlessly means without bounds, so the outer letters of better go

explanation.surface: A band plays better after a couple of pints.
explanation.definitionFit: A quartette is a group of four musicians, small by orchestral standards.

clue.text: A Greek put wager on this sequence of letters

parts.note: alpha is a Greek letter
a wager is a bet

explanation.surface: A Greek gambles on something.
explanation.definitionFit: The alphabet is the standard ordered set of letters of a writing system.

clue.text: Space for the French chap walking down the aisle

parts.note: le is French for the
a bridegroom walks down the aisle at his wedding

explanation.surface: Room is needed for the bridegroom at a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Legroom is the space available for a seated person's legs.

clue.text: English sheep raised with horse

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: English sheep bred alongside a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare is a female horse.

clue.text: Strip and run about naked

definitions.meaning: a strip of colour is a ... or stripe
to run naked through a public place, as at a sports match

explanation.surface: Undressing and dashing about nude.

clue.text: Suits an abandoned bear?

indicators.note: abandoned suggests the letters are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: Clothing fit for a bear left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain is to bear or endure something.

clue.text: A broken grey line in patterned sock

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A grey stripe gone wrong on a diamond-patterned sock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges GREY with L (line) to give RGYLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An Argyle sock bears the Scottish diamond pattern.

clue.text: Domesticity-bound direction taken by Gray's ploughman on Sunday

explanation.surface: A poetic ploughman heads back to the farmhouse on the Sabbath.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gray's 'Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard' opens with the ploughman plodding his way back to his house.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading towards one's house means travelling towards domestic life.

clue.text: Army doctor starts to look at rifleman's tooth

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

indicators.note: starts to picks the opening letters of the two words that follow

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rifleman

explanation.surface: A military medic inspects a soldier's teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A molar is a back grinding tooth.

clue.text: Perched next to younger sex-mad Greek god

parts.note: a bird that perched sat
YR is the abbreviation for younger

explanation.surface: A lustful deity sits beside a junior companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Satyrs were lustful woodland deities, half man and half goat, in Greek myth.

clue.text: It's quite expensive to soak

definitions.meaning: a ... price is a high one
to soak in liquid, as with tea

explanation.surface: A remark that soaking is pricey.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep describes a price that is high, and to steep means to immerse in liquid.

clue.text: Live, lust and join in

parts.note: to live or exist is to be
to lust after is to long for

explanation.surface: A recipe for life: exist, desire, and take part.
explanation.definitionFit: To belong is to be a member and fit in with a group.

clue.text: Records an attempt on the wall at Bayeux perhaps

definitions.text: on the wall at Bayeux perhaps

parts.note: to record is to tape, so records are tapes
an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: Logging an effort to scale the castle wall in Normandy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bayeux Tapestry, depicting the Norman Conquest, hangs on display in Bayeux, Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bayeux Tapestry is the famous embroidered hanging, an example of woven wall art.

clue.text: The tailless marsh-plant bird

indicators.note: tailless means the final letter of the word The is cut off

parts.note: a rush is a plant growing in marshes

explanation.surface: A strange bird lacking a tail, found among reeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrush is a songbird, such as the song thrush.

clue.text: Not bikini-style but old and strangely epicene

indicators.note: strangely signals the letters of epicene are rearranged

explanation.surface: A swimsuit described as dated and oddly sexless.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-piece swimsuit is a single garment, unlike a two-part bikini.
